title: "Full-Text Search Index"

## Overview

RDFLib.jl includes a built-in full-text search index for finding RDF triples by literal text content. The `TextIndex` tokenizes literal values and builds an inverted index, supporting exact matches, prefix wildcards, and multi-token queries.

```{julia}
using RDFLib
```

## Creating a TextIndex

Build a text index from an existing graph.

```{julia}
# Build a graph with textual data
g = RDFGraph()
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
foaf = Namespace("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/")
dc = Namespace("http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/")
bind!(g, "ex", ex)
bind!(g, "foaf", foaf)
bind!(g, "dc", dc)

# People
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), foaf("name"), Literal("Alice Smith")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), dc("description"), Literal("A software engineer specializing in machine learning")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), foaf("name"), Literal("Bob Johnson")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), dc("description"), Literal("A data scientist working on natural language processing")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("carol"), foaf("name"), Literal("Carol Williams")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("carol"), dc("description"), Literal("A machine learning researcher at the university")))

# Publications
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper1"), dc("title"), Literal("Introduction to Machine Learning Algorithms")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper1"), dc("creator"), ex("alice")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper2"), dc("title"), Literal("Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper2"), dc("creator"), ex("bob")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper3"), dc("title"), Literal("Advanced Statistical Methods for Data Science")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper3"), dc("creator"), ex("carol")))

println("Graph has $(length(g)) triples")
```

```{julia}
# Create a text index from the graph
idx = TextIndex(g)
println("Text index created: ", typeof(idx))
```

## Full-Text Search Queries

Search for triples whose literal values contain specific terms.

```{julia}
# Search for a single term
results = text_search(idx, "machine")
println("Results for 'machine':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

```{julia}
# Search is case-insensitive
results = text_search(idx, "ALICE")
println("Results for 'ALICE':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

## Multi-Token Search

Multiple tokens are combined with AND — all must be present in the literal.

```{julia}
# Both tokens must appear in the same literal
results = text_search(idx, "machine learning")
println("Results for 'machine learning' (AND):")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

```{julia}
# More specific multi-token query
results = text_search(idx, "natural language")
println("Results for 'natural language':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

## Wildcard / Prefix Search

Use `*` at the end of a term for prefix matching.

```{julia}
# Prefix search: find anything starting with "mach"
results = text_search(idx, "mach*")
println("Results for 'mach*':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

```{julia}
# Prefix search for names starting with "al"
results = text_search(idx, "al*")
println("Results for 'al*':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

## Limiting Results

Control the number of results returned.

```{julia}
# Limit to top 2 results
results = text_search(idx, "learning"; limit=2)
println("Top 2 results for 'learning':")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

## Building and Rebuilding the Index

Use `build!` to index a graph or re-index after changes.

```{julia}
# Add new data
add!(g, Triple(ex("paper4"), dc("title"), Literal("Machine Learning in Healthcare Applications")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("dave"), foaf("name"), Literal("Dave Miller")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("dave"), dc("description"), Literal("A healthcare data analyst")))

# Rebuild the index to include new triples
idx2 = TextIndex()
build!(idx2, g)

# Now the new data is searchable
results = text_search(idx2, "healthcare")
println("Results for 'healthcare' (after rebuild):")
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject, " — ", t.object)
end
```

## Integration with SPARQL via CONTAINS_TEXT

Set a global text index for use in SPARQL queries with the `CONTAINS_TEXT` filter function.

```{julia}
# Set the global text index
set_text_index!(idx2)

# Use CONTAINS_TEXT in SPARQL FILTER
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?paper ?title WHERE {
        ?paper dc:title ?title .
        FILTER(CONTAINS_TEXT(?title, "learning"))
    }
""")
println("Papers about 'learning':")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:paper], " — ", row[:title])
end
```

```{julia}
# Combine text search with graph traversal
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?author_name ?title WHERE {
        ?paper dc:title ?title .
        ?paper dc:creator ?author .
        ?author foaf:name ?author_name .
        FILTER(CONTAINS_TEXT(?title, "machine"))
    }
""")
println("Authors of 'machine' papers:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:author_name], " wrote: ", row[:title])
end
```

```{julia}
# Clean up the global index when done
clear_text_index!()
```

## Summary

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `TextIndex()` | Create empty index |
| `TextIndex(g)` | Build index from graph |
| `build!(idx, g)` | Build/rebuild index from graph |
| `text_search(idx, query)` | Search for matching triples |
| `text_search(idx, query; limit=n)` | Search with result limit |
| `set_text_index!(idx)` | Set global index for SPARQL |
| `clear_text_index!()` | Clear global index |

**Query syntax:**

| Pattern | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `"word"` | Exact token match | `text_search(idx, "alice")` |
| `"word*"` | Prefix wildcard | `text_search(idx, "mach*")` |
| `"word1 word2"` | AND (all tokens) | `text_search(idx, "machine learning")` |
